response.text:
Stubb and Flask, mounted on the forecastle bulwarks, passed additional lashings over the hanging anchors. “No, Stubb; you may pound that knot as much as you please, but you’ll never pound into me what you were just now saying. Didn’t you once say that whatever ship Ahab sails in should pay something extra on its insurance, as if loaded with powder aft and lucifers forward?” “Well, suppose I did? I’ve part changed my flesh—why not my mind? And supposing we are loaded with powder aft and lucifers forward; how could the lucifers get afire in this drenching spray? Why, my little man, you have pretty red hair, but you couldn’t get afire now. Shake yourself; you’re Aquarius, or the water-bearer, Flask; might fill pitchers at your coat collar. For extra risks the companies have extra guarantees—here are hydrants. And what’s the mighty difference between holding a mast’s lightning-rod in a storm, and standing by a mast that hasn’t any? Don’t you see, you timber-head, that no harm can come to the holder of the rod unless the mast is first struck? Not one ship in a hundred carries rods; we were in no more danger than other crews. Would you have every man go about with a small lightning-rod up his hat, like a militia officer’s skewered feather, and trailing behind like his sash. Why don’t ye be sensible, Flask? Any man with half an eye can be sensible.” “I don’t know that, Stubb. You sometimes find it rather hard.” “Yes; when a fellow’s soaked through, it’s hard to be sensible, that’s a fact.”

“Seems we lash these anchors as if never to be used again,” said Stubb. “Tying them is like tying a man’s hands; what big generous hands they are—iron fists! I wonder if the world is anchored anywhere; if she is, she swings with an uncommon long cable. Wring out my jacket skirts, will ye? A long-tailed coat in storms carries off the water. Same with cocked hats: cocks form gable-end eave-troughs. No more monkey-jackets and tarpaulins for me; I’ll mount a swallow-tail and drive down a beaver.” “Halloa! whew! there goes my tarpaulin overboard; Lord, Lord, that the winds that come from heaven should be so unmannerly! This is a nasty night, lad.”
